analysis:
The only change in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift is at head lines 795-797. The text-path call to ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize now also passes promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil. requestCacheScope is derived at lines 428-429 from the authenticated coordinator cacheScope. For diffusion models with an empty cacheScope it falls back to nativeLocalCacheScope. The new argument partitions prompt-token reuse by the same scope as the prefix KV cache (T-041 / SEC-035). When the cache is disabled (cacheEnabled=false, a legacy coordinator without authenticated scope) it passes nil, which should disable cross-request token reuse. This looks like a tightening: a token-reuse cache keyed per scope or disabled, matching the scoping of cacheSalt. The edit does not touch the media path (which passes cacheScope to submitTokenized separately), the lease handling, or the release paths. I could not see the implementation of ProviderPromptContractPipeline.tokenize, so these points are unverified:
- Whether nil truly bypasses any prompt-token cache.
- Whether an empty-string scope (a local HTTP engine with cacheScope "" and cacheEnabled true) shares reuse across local callers. That was already the case for the KV cache and is the accepted single-tenant local scoping.
- Whether the scope is hashed before being stored or logged, so no raw scope or tenant identifier is exposed.
These should be checked in the pipeline's tokenize implementation and its token-cache tests. No regression was identified in the supplied lines.
